title: DHW-path space multi-start anchors its seeds on the smooth guess, not the thermostat demand: two-zone DHW plans miss the basin
claim: On the two-zone DHW solve at winter_typical and winter_moderate prices, the plan HeatPumpOptimizer._solve_space ships scores 1.043 and 1.066 objective units (1.18 % and 1.00 %) above a feasible plan the same call reaches from one extra bang-bang seed, and the gap closes to 0.285 at winter_typical when that call gets the space-only path's thermostat-anchored seeds.
mechanism: _optimize_space_only builds its bang-bang seeds from baseline_energy, the energy of the thermostat reference (_compute_baseline_power), and adds _DEEP_LOW_ENERGY_START_FRACTION on two-zone. _solve_space (the DHW path, through _relaxed_plans) builds them from energy = sum(min(init_base, headroom))*dt, where init_base is the smooth price guess p_max*0.6*weights clipped to [0.5 p_min, 0.8 p_max]: on winter_typical two-zone that is 51.2 kWh against the 68.5 kWh the shipped plan uses, so its 0.35x anchor sits at 17.4 kWh, and it has no thermostat seed and no deep anchor. The winning challenger seed is bang-bang at 0.35 x the plan's own energy (24 kWh), which no DHW-path candidate brackets.

evidence.contention_note: two other finder seats running; the value is an objective difference, contention-immune

title: Charged wood tank zeroes 4 of 5 space-only multi-start seeds; mild two-zone days ship the all-off plan
claim: On a two-tank (wood) two-zone house without DHW, HeatPumpOptimizer's space-only solve hands _multi_start_minimize 4 all-zero starts of 5 in 32 of the 60 cells of this seat's axis, and on the 5 mild 24 h cells it ships a 0 kWh plan that a one-run challenger beats by 1.47-2.03 objective units with no feasibility loss.
mechanism: optimizer.py (space-only path, ~line 5507): seed_power = baseline_power * (1 - _wood_covered_share(...)); a tank that covers the thermostat reference gives share 1.0, so seed_power, baseline_energy and the three _price_ranked_start vectors built from baseline_energy (full, low, deep-low) are all zero. Only the price-weighted initial guess is live, and the all-off point is a stationary basin for the relaxed descent (the start term is not in the relaxed objective, and a run below the 1 kW floor is clipped by the candidate stage), so the multi-start has no start inside the one-run basin the true objective prefers.

title: No all-off start: negative-price storage plants ship plans 1.8-8.6 % worse than off; MPC masks most
claim: On the 60 d0-grid cells summer_negative/summer_warm/*, production ships on 16 (every one a storage plant: valve-storage, wood, manual-valve-buffer, flow-setpoint-behind-valve; 0 of 12 plain) a space plan whose true objective exceeds the plan production's own _multi_start_minimize reaches from the all-off (lower-bound) start by 273-3204 objective units (1.8-7.4 % of the objective), heating an above-ceiling house 2.9-35.6 more degree-steps for 0.03-1.65 SEK of negative-price revenue; on the 60 flat-price twins the gap is 0. D0.M6: in a 24 h closed loop re-planned hourly (loop.py, plant == model, production's warm seed), the augmented arm (structured seeds incl. the lower bound) realises < 1 objective unit better on 12 of the 16 gap cells, 30-85 units better on 3 (all flow-setpoint-behind-valve) and 128 units worse on 1; mean realised gap 1.59 units/day, -3.95 with the most favourable cell dropped, energy money within 0.75 SEK/day either way: the shipped (published) plan is wrong, the realised loss is small and not robust.
mechanism: Every production start set (_solve_space and the space-only path in optimizer.py: the guess, _price_ranked_start at the baseline/low/deep-low energy, headroom*0.5, the seed power) carries energy, and none is the lower bound. Through a buffer and mixing valve the room's response to pump power saturates: past a small threshold extra power no longer raises the room (the overshoot penalty is flat in power: J at 0.5x and 1.0x the shipped plan differ by 0.3 units, at 0.01x it is the off value), while the negative price keeps paying for more. Every start descends onto that plateau, so L-BFGS-B never sees the off basin the objective prefers by thousands of units. Masking: the shipped plan's heating sits after step 0 (step0_prod = 0 on every gap cell), so a re-plan an hour later re-derives it and the closed loop on most cells coasts at the off trajectory anyway.

title: _terminal_cost docstring: no credit breaches the tail floor; at any learnable weight it never does
claim: With HeatPumpOptimizer._terminal_cost zeroed, the shipped plan's last-2-h degree-steps below the per-step comfort floor are no worse than with it on 0 of 40 committed cells at the default comfort_weight (5.0) and 0 of 40 at the comfort learner's minimum (1.0), while tail energy falls on 40/40 and 39/40; the floor-breach half of the docstring holds only at comfort_weight 0.05 (13 of 40), outside what comfort_learning can reach. On every d0-grid line (2400, decomp_oracle.py) zeroing the credit moves 1811 plans and lowers tail energy on 1659, and worsens the tail floor breach on 0.
mechanism: The comfort floor is held by the objective's own floor terms (_comfort_terms: squared undershoot x10 plus the L1 term _COMFORT_FLOOR_L1 x comfort_weight), which at any learnable weight (comfort_learning.COMFORT_WEIGHT_MIN..MAX = 1..40) already price a tail undershoot above the energy the credit would save. Removing the credit does dump the last hours (tail kWh 3.6-10.7 -> 0), but the room coasts down without crossing the floor inside the horizon. The docstring states the floor breach as the reason the term exists; a reader (or a fixer weighing a change to the credit) is told the credit guards comfort when it guards only the end-state value.

title: HA stop mid-solve raises a persistent solve_worker_fallback repair that no later solve ever clears
claim: When EVENT_HOMEASSISTANT_STOP fires while a solve's reply is being read from the process worker, the reap breaks the pipe, _await_optimize takes the fallback route (one in-process GIL solve during the stop) and raises the persistent 'solve_worker_fallback' repair; after a restart the issue is still raised once the new instance has solved twice through a healthy worker (count 1, null control 0).
mechanism: _shutdown_process_pool kills the child before taking the lock (by design, D1-s2-05), so the in-flight _run_in_process reads EOF and raises ProcessWorkerUnavailable('Ran out of input'); _await_optimize treats that like a broken install: _note_worker_fallback creates the issue with is_persistent=True and reruns the solve in process. The issue is cleared only by _clear_worker_fallback, which returns early unless THIS process's _WORKER_FALLBACK_CAUSES latched a cause for the entry; after the restart the module dict is empty, so every successful solve leaves the restored issue in place. HA does not unload entries at stop, so _release_registrations' clear does not run either.

evidence.unit: stale solve_worker_fallback issues after restart
evidence.machine: box B4 container, linux x86_64, Python 3.14 venv-ci
evidence.contention_note: part B of m4_race.py and other finder seats running on the box; a count, contention-immune; thread_factor is the residual after subtracting executor-thread CPU (rl.DELIBERATE)

instrumented_symbol: heatpump_optimizer.coordinator:_clear_worker_fallback (with _await_optimize, _note_worker_fallback, async_register_worker_shutdown._stop driven on a real loop)

perturbation.change: _clear_worker_fallback deletes the issue whenever no cause is latched in this process (drop the early return after the pop); harness flag --perturb

metric_definition: Count of hass.issues entries with issue_id solve_worker_fallback after the restarted instance completed two successful process-route solves.
phenomenon_property: A repair notice raised for a transient, self-inflicted cause (the instance's own stop reaping its worker) must not be raised persistent, or must be withdrawable by the next healthy solve in a fresh process; a stop must not rerun the killed solve in process.
seam_rule: grep -n 'is_persistent=True' custom_components/heatpump_optimizer/*.py  (each persistent issue: is its clear path reachable from a fresh process?)

proposed_fix_scope: coordinator.py: mark the stop (a module flag set by _stop) so a reply broken by our own reap is not a worker fault (no issue, no in-process rerun during stop); and/or let _clear_worker_fallback delete the issue when no entry has a latched cause in this process.

title: tests/harness.py lifecycle helpers skip HA's on_unload processing: 1 shutdown per unload (HA 2), 4 leaks per NotReady (HA 0)
claim: The suite's entry-manager instrument diverges from Home Assistant's ConfigEntry in two seams of one mechanism (_async_process_on_unload): ha_unload_entry calls each async_on_unload callback FIFO and drops a returned coroutine, so HeatPumpOptimizerCoordinator.async_shutdown runs once per unload where HA runs it twice (1 RuntimeWarning per unload; store saves 3 vs 4 per unload); and ha_setup_entry runs no unload callback when async_setup_entry raises ConfigEntryNotReady, so each failed attempt leaves 4 live registrations reaching its coordinator and the coordinator alive (3 of 3 after 3 failures), where HA's order leaves 0 and 0.
mechanism: homeassistant ConfigEntry._async_process_on_unload: `while self._on_unload: if job := self._on_unload.pop()(): self.async_create_task(hass, job)` then awaits the tasks; the stub DataUpdateCoordinator registers `config_entry.async_on_unload(self.async_shutdown)` as upstream does; tests/harness.py:ha_unload_entry runs `callback()` and drops the result. Every suite test unloading through it therefore never runs the second HeatPumpOptimizerCoordinator.async_shutdown (pump_arbiter.release -> _persist a second time, legionella release, forget_held) that a real unload runs. On ConfigEntryNotReady HA's ConfigEntry.async_setup also awaits _async_process_on_unload (the coordinator's own _release_registrations and the base-class async_shutdown), which tests/harness.py:ha_setup_entry never runs: production's #236 cleanup is therefore unobservable through the suite's helper, and a test that counts registrations after a NotReady sees leaks HA would not have.

title: A user write landing during a debounced in-flight solve is dropped: plan ignores it until the next interval
claim: When away, economy mode, a manual plan, a comfort-weight reset or a holiday-calendar change is written while a solve started through async_request_refresh (setup's first solve, a button, a service, any state listener) is in flight, the write's re-plan request is dropped by the refresh debouncer and the published plan stays built on the pre-write value until the next scheduled update: 7 of 8 request-refresh census rows stale, 0 of 8 when the in-flight solve came from async_refresh.
mechanism: DataUpdateCoordinator.async_request_refresh goes through Debouncer.async_call, which returns without arming a trailing run while a call is executing (upstream: 'Locked means a call is in progress. Any call is good, so abort.'; the stub mirrors it). The in-flight call is the refresh carrying the solve, so the writer's request never reaches async_run_optimization, whose #1754 re-run latch (_optimization_rerun_requested) only catches calls that arrive there. The scheduled interval refresh bypasses the debouncer, so the same write during a scheduled solve IS re-planned (null control). The stale window is up to one optimization_interval (default 30 min, DEFAULT_OPTIMIZATION_INTERVAL); _mode_superseded covers only the fixed modes.

title: Store-load boundary passes NaN: a "NaN" leaf reaches the live model and makes the next save undecodable
claim: store._poisoned returns False for float('nan') and for the string "NaN" (abs(nan) >= ABSURD is False), so QuarantiningStore.async_load hands those leaves to the loaders; in 3 of 515 single-leaf "NaN" substitutions over every d1-stores healthy payload the NaN reaches the live thermal model or the published payload, and in the same 3 the next save writes a bare NaN token that the following restart's orjson load refuses, dropping the whole accuracy and snapshots documents.
mechanism: _poisoned's float branch is `abs(value) >= ABSURD`; NaN compares False, so _sanitize keeps it although the module and _poisoned's own docstring say non-finite is quarantined. comfort_learning's from_dict reads `float(np.clip(float('NaN'), lo, hi))` = nan (np.clip propagates NaN) into learned_weight/evidence, published as data['comfort_learning']; DhwProfileLearner.apply_cooling_rate does the same into ThermalParameters.dhw_cooling_rate (the solver's input). The accuracy and snapshot savers then json.dumps the NaN as a bare token; Home Assistant's orjson load refuses it and moves the whole file aside, so the learned accuracy history and the snapshots are lost at the next restart. tests/finite_boundary.py's own module-level checks 'the boundary quarantines nan at every depth' and 'str-nan' print FAIL on this tree.

evidence.unit: leaves (of 515) whose NaN reaches the live model/published payload; same 3 make a stored document undecodable
evidence.contention_note: fan-out: other finder seats and this seat's fuzz shards running; a count, contention-immune

perturbation.change: --fix: store._poisoned also returns True for a non-finite float or a string whose float() is non-finite (one line: `return not math.isfinite(value) or abs(value) >= ABSURD`), patched in memory

metric_definition: Count of single numeric leaves which, set to the string "NaN" and loaded through the real loaders plus one cycle, leave a non-finite value live/published or an undecodable store document.
phenomenon_property: No store load hands a loader a non-finite number in any spelling (float NaN/inf, or a string float() turns into one); every non-finite leaf is quarantined at QuarantiningStore.async_load, so nothing non-finite is installed live or re-saved.
seam_rule: PYTHONPATH=tests/hastub python3 dev/audit/rounds/round11/D1/s2/nan_boundary.py  (every numeric leaf of every d1-stores payload; the seam is store._poisoned, one function)

proposed_fix_scope: store.py:_poisoned refuses non-finite floats (math.isfinite); add a NaN arm to tests/finite_boundary.py's run (its own module-level check already fails).

title: PV production is read with no age check: a silent or future-stamped meter still seeds step 0 and is published
claim: HeatPumpOptimizerCoordinator._pv_measured_production reads CONF_PV_PRODUCTION_ENTITY through hass.states.get + state_power_kw, never through InputReader, so the 30-minute limit const.INPUT_MAX_AGE_MINUTES[CONF_PV_PRODUCTION_ENTITY] declares is never applied: in 6 of 6 report ages past the limit (31 min to 24 h) and for a report stamped 90 min in the future, the real cycle publishes data['pv']['measured_production_kw']=5.0 and overwrites step 0 of the PV forecast with it.
mechanism: _pv_forecast sets production[0] = min(self._pv_production, peak_kw) from _pv_measured_production, which is `state_power_kw(self.hass.states.get(entity_id), sign='clamp')`. state_power_kw's own docstring calls itself 'the one parse of a power state outside InputReader (which adds the staleness of a configured input)'; the slot has a declared limit (const.py: INPUT_MAX_AGE_MINUTES[CONF_PV_PRODUCTION_ENTITY] = 30.0, INPUT_ON_CHANGE_MAX_AGE_MINUTES pv_production_entity 30.0) that no reader of it applies, and the slot never appears in the input watchdog (staleness.py: 'unread'). An inverter whose integration drops off mid-afternoon keeps the planner believing in its last output (here 5 kW) for the current step indefinitely, and a host clock stepped back makes the same reading look fresh.

title: A weather forecast that stopped advancing is read as a recovery: published fresh while every row lies in the past
claim: _fetch_weather treats any non-empty plausible get_forecasts reply as a successful fetch (_weather_fetch_recovered clears _weather_stale_since) without checking that its rows reach now, so in 5 of 5 cells where the provider keeps returning the same 48 rows and the clock is 1 to 48 h past the last row, the real cycle publishes weather_forecast_stale_hours=None (fresh) while the plan's outdoor array is the last row's 0.7 C held flat (the live weather entity says -3.0 C).
mechanism: coordinator._plausible_forecast_rows filters non-dict rows and out-of-window field values only; a stale-but-well-formed forecast passes, `if forecast_data:` takes the success branch and calls _weather_fetch_recovered, which sets _weather_stale_since=None. _forecast_arrays then extrapolates the last row across the horizon. The empty-forecast and exception branches do mark the data stale (price_weather.py: weather_empty_hidden=0), so the staleness signal exists and only this branch skips it. A weather integration that stops refreshing its forecast (a cached provider, an expired API key that keeps serving the last answer) leaves the plan on a days-old trajectory while the published freshness says nothing is wrong.

evidence.unit: cells (of 5) with every forecast row in the past published as fresh (stale_hours None)
evidence.contention_note: fan-out, other seats running; a count

perturbation.change: --fix: coordinator._plausible_forecast_rows also drops a row whose hour (datetime + 1 h) has ended, patched in memory, so an all-past reply is an empty one and takes the existing stale branch

metric_definition: Of 5 cells 1/6/12/24/48 h past the last row of a non-advancing forecast, cycles publishing weather_forecast_stale_hours None.
phenomenon_property: A feed reply that does not cover now is not a fresh fetch: the forecast's staleness (weather_forecast_stale_hours) is set whenever the forecast the plan stands on no longer reaches the current step, whatever branch delivered it.
seam_rule: PYTHONPATH=tests/hastub python3 dev/audit/rounds/round11/D1/s2/price_weather.py  (each external feed's success branch -- weather, Tibber, price entity -- driven with a reply that no longer covers now; the price feeds hold, weather does not)

title: off_restore._armed_record marks loaded before its read lands: a concurrent caller sees no hold and saves that
claim: off_restore._armed_record sets held.loaded = True before awaiting load_mapping and takes no lock, so a second caller while the first read is in flight gets an empty armed set: with the persisted record holding the heat curve's baseline (3.0) and async_armed_entry's read pending, async_restore (entering MODE_OFF, or unload) sends 0 restore writes instead of 1 and saves {"armed": {}}, which QuarantiningStore.async_save writes after the read lands -- so the hold is not released now and the baseline is gone from disk for the next restart (2 of 2 consequences; 0 when the two calls are serial).
mechanism: QuarantiningStore.async_save waits for the read in flight, but _save(held) builds its payload from held.armed before calling it, so the store-level wait cannot help: the payload is the pre-read empty set. The sibling with the same 'loaded before the await' shape, pump_arbiter._load, is safe because both its callers (apply, the switch-on pass) hold held.lock; off_restore has no lock and five public entry points (async_arm, async_restore, async_armed_entry, async_rebaseline, async_consumer_state) reach _armed_record from the heat-curve publish, the pump arbiter, set_mode and unload, which run as separate loop tasks. The exposure is the first read of an entry's record after a start: a set_mode('off')/unload, or a second consumer, landing while the first cycle's heat-curve arm is reading.

evidence.unit: consequences of 2 (restore not sent; armed baseline missing from the saved document)
evidence.contention_note: fan-out, other seats running; a count (the read suspension is a fixed 10 ms sleep, the ordering is deterministic)

instrumented_symbol: custom_components/heatpump_optimizer/off_restore.py:_armed_record (driven through off_restore.async_armed_entry and off_restore.async_restore on one entry, real QuarantiningStore)

perturbation.change: --fix: _armed_record wrapped so one read per record is shared and every concurrent caller awaits it (loaded only after the read), patched in memory
perturbation.observed_value: consequences=0: restore_writes_sent=1 (set_value 3 on number.curve), as in the serial control

metric_definition: Count of {restore write not sent, armed baseline absent from the saved document} when async_restore runs while another caller's first read of the off-restore record is pending.
phenomenon_property: No caller of a lazily loaded persisted record observes it before its read lands, and no save of that record can carry a payload built before the read: the first read is shared and awaited by every caller.
seam_rule: grep -nE '\.loaded = True|_loaded = True' custom_components/heatpump_optimizer/*.py  (each lazy-load flag set before its await; safe only where every caller holds one lock, as pump_arbiter's held.lock does)

title: One wrong-typed numeric option in an earlier-version config entry fails setup or every cycle, with no quarantine
claim: async_migrate_entry only stamps the version, and ThermalParameters.from_config / _tabled_values / _flow_curve_values and comfort_band.effective read numeric options raw (no coercion, or a bare float()), so of 1200 seeded single-option mutants of a healthy all-features entry stamped v1..v6, 54 make the coordinator constructor raise (setup fails) and 88 make both cycles raise UpdateFailed (every update fails) -- 142 permanent failures, 21 to 26 per version -- with nothing logged as a quarantined option and no reset.
mechanism: _tabled_values copies ~50 numeric options straight from the entry (`config.get(KEY, DEFAULT)`, no float()), with the comment 'Booleans are coerced because a config entry may carry a string' -- numbers are not; a string or null dhw_tank_volume then raises in dhw_tank_thermal_mass on every cycle ('can't multiply sequence by non-int of type float'). from_config's own float(config.get(CONF_MAX_TEMP ...)) and _flow_curve_values' float(config.get(CONF_TARGET_TEMP ...)) raise in the constructor on '', 'abc', None, a list or a dict; comfort_band.effective's float(candidate.get(...)) raises on every cycle for min_temperature. An entity slot holding a list/dict raises as an unhashable key in InputReader._begin on every cycle. Because the migration validates nothing, an entry written by an older release (or a hand-edited core.config_entries) with one such value never loads until the user edits the option.

title: A stored boosted_h past timedelta's range raises in the boost restore task on every restart
claim: boost._restore_settle builds timedelta(hours=boosted_h) for any finite non-negative boosted_h, and store.ABSURD (1e15) admits values far past timedelta's range, so for 4 of 5 stored values (3e10, 1e11, 1e12, 1e14 h) the restore task the coordinator spawns raises OverflowError on both of two restarts (8 of 10), leaving the running space overlay's start (space_since) unrestored and the boosted time at timedelta(0) instead of the 'unknown' (None) the loader's own comment prescribes; the fifth (1e10 h) loads as ~47 000 years.
mechanism: The guard `isinstance(hours, (int, float)) and 0.0 <= hours < math.inf` accepts any finite hours; held.space_settle_until is set before the timedelta call, so the raise leaves a half-applied restore and skips the space since/end handling below it; the exception escapes the spawned restore_session task (Home Assistant logs 'Task exception was never retrieved' each start). The document is not rewritten by the failed restore, so the same failure recurs at every restart until a later boost overwrites the store. DOMAINS declares the field `space_settle/boosted_h: _Z0`, which only the debug-level off-domain diagnostic reads.

evidence.contention_note: fan-out, other seats running; a count

title: Pump flag slots read a non-finite state (nan, inf, 1e309) as True: fault and defrost fabricated
claim: inputs.parse_bool reads the states 'nan', 'NaN', 'inf', '-inf' and '1e309' as True (float(token) != 0.0), so a heat-pump fault or defrost entity reporting a non-finite number publishes fault=True and defrosting=True and freezes learning with freeze_reason 'pump_fault', where the numeric reader refuses the same state.
mechanism: pump_signals.read -> InputReader.read_bool -> inputs.parse_bool: the numeric arm `return float(token) != 0.0` is reached for any token outside BOOL_TRUE/BOOL_FALSE, and float('nan') != 0.0 and float('inf') != 0.0 are both True. No finiteness test precedes it (const.finite_float, the integration's own number rule, refuses non-finite values), so an unreadable numeric state becomes a positive flag rather than `not_boolean`. The fabricated fault freezes every learner (`_learning_frozen`); the fabricated defrost feeds the defrost window/duty fold and blocks the COP fold.

title: An Open-Meteo sample stamped 0001-01-01 fails every solve: IrradianceSeries.mean_over overflows outside the fence
claim: _parse_block keeps a sample stamped '0001-01-01T00:00', and IrradianceSeries.mean_over then raises OverflowError on `t - self.resolution` for every plan step, so every solve fails ('Optimization failed: date value out of range') for as long as the series is held, with last_update_success staying True.

title: _run_in_process's transport-failure arm waits unbounded on a killed worker while holding _PROCESS_LOCK
claim: When the job write or reply read fails with a transport error (BrokenPipeError and kin), _run_in_process calls worker.kill() then worker.wait() with no timeout inside `with _PROCESS_LOCK`, so a child the kill does not end at once never returns and the lock stays held, while the sibling ProcessWorkerTimeout arm bounds the same wait with _SHUTDOWN_LOCK_TIMEOUT_S for exactly that child.
mechanism: coordinator.py `_run_in_process`: the `except Exception as err` arm (transport, never the job) does `worker.kill(); worker.wait()`; the `except ProcessWorkerTimeout` arm above it does `worker.kill(); worker.wait(timeout=_SHUTDOWN_LOCK_TIMEOUT_S)` with the comment 'a child the kill does not end at once (one stuck in the kernel) must not turn this into the same unbounded wait'. One fact (how long to wait for a killed child) decided twice. Held, the lock wedges every later solve, replay and sensor-advisor job behind it (each parks an executor thread in `with _PROCESS_LOCK`), and the awaiting refresh never completes, so last_update_success never turns False. The same unbounded wait sits in _shutdown_process_pool's at_exit arm (coordinator.py ~1917).

evidence.unit: RESULT transport_lock_held_after (1 = _PROCESS_LOCK still held after the 8 s cap; transport_returned_within_cap=0)
evidence.machine: orchestrator Mac, Apple M1 (darwin arm64, 8 cores), shared box
evidence.contention_note: fan-out running; the cap is a deadline 160x the bounded arm's return, not a timing RESULT

perturbation.change: the transport arm's `worker.wait()` becomes `worker.wait(timeout=_SHUTDOWN_LOCK_TIMEOUT_S)` (`--perturb`, the function recompiled in memory from its own source)

title: A persistently failing store save is logged only at DEBUG at all 17 persist handlers; state stops persisting
claim: Every persist handler (17, persist_seams.py) catches any exception from building and saving its store payload and logs it only at DEBUG; with the save body forced to fail on every pass across setup, two refreshes, unload, restart and a refresh, each of the 10 handlers the lifecycle reaches added zero WARNING-or-higher records, so a payload-builder bug or a failing save silently stops the ledger, accuracy, thermal-learning, price-model, snapshot, away, legionella, notifier, off-restore and energy stores from persisting until a restart loses the unsaved state.
mechanism: Pattern `try: await store.async_save(<payload built inline>) except Exception as err: _LOGGER.debug('Could not persist ...: %s', err)` in coordinator._async_save_{thermal_learning,price_model,ledger,accuracy,energy_totals,manual_plan,snapshots}, away.persist_override, boost.persist, dhw_learning.async_save_{profile,draws}, duty_switch._persist, legionella.async_save, notifier._async_save, off_restore._save, pump_arbiter._persist, debugger.DebugCollector.async_save. The payload is built inside the try, so a programming error in any learner's as_dict (an AttributeError, a non-serialisable value) is caught with the transport failures and logged below Home Assistant's default level on every cycle; nothing latches it (log_held exists for exactly this) and no repair issue is raised.

evidence.unit: persist handlers (of 10 reached) whose persistent save failure added no WARNING+ record

title: Mode-less counter-metered pump: an unplanned hot-water charge folds into the house learner as space heat

title: The yield instrument's verdict population is not the review rounds the verdict bus records: 42 rounds missing, 9 counted twice
claim: Over the 234 merges of v7.1.10..92d38ecb, policy_lint.mjs --stats (fetchWindow + statsHistogram, comments and reviews) reads 420 verdict comments, while the verdict bus holds 452 distinct (PR, word, head) verdicts: 42 bus verdicts (24 blocked, over 32 PRs, every head an ancestor of the merged branch) never reached the PR as a comment or review, and 9 comments are second relays of one verdict (same bus-nonce), so rounds per merge reads 2.039 where the bus population read once gives 2.178, one-round yield 0.476 where it gives 0.452, and #3618 (a fix lane with a bus merge verdict) reads as a merge carrying no verdict.
mechanism: A reviewer's verdict is written to the bus (review/<pr>, verdict/<pr>, archived as archive/review/<pr>) and relayed to the PR as an hpo-approver comment; the relay delivered some verdicts never (42, including a cluster written to the bus 2026-11-14 10:45-11:45) and some twice (9, identical bus-nonce, hours apart). fetchWindow reads only /issues/<n>/comments and /pulls/<n>/reviews, and statsHistogram counts every parsable comment as one round; review_strength.py reads the bus. The two in-tree verdict readers therefore count different populations of the same rounds, and the brief's rule (comment or review) inherits the comment side's gaps.

title: Push-mode pump flags quiet past their 30/60 min on-change limit publish Input Problem on a healthy pump
claim: With the six pump-flag inputs configured as report-on-change sources that legitimately hold their value for 255 min, one real coordinator cycle publishes all six in stale_inputs and turns the Input Problem binary sensor on; the same flags changed 10 min ago, or re-reported 1 min ago, publish none.
mechanism: INPUT_ON_CHANGE_MAX_AGE_MINUTES keeps the polling limit (30 min defrost/online/backup/booster/capacity-limited, 60 min fault) for the pump flags, on the barrier's disposition 'fails safe'. That reason covers the control consequence (a stale flag demotes to None). It does not cover the reader's other consequence: InputHealth.stale_keys feeds payload stale_inputs, and InputHealthBinarySensor.is_on reads it. const.py's own comment says the reference integration's MQTT push mode 'does not poll at all -- it pushes on change', and a defrost flag 'off' through a mild day or an online flag 'on' for days is the legitimate quiet interval the class names. claim: The self-test's step-1a3 extraction (sed from '# --- 1a3.' to '# --- 1b0.') now ends inside the open `if [ -n "$REUSE" ]; then ... else` that was inserted before 1b0, so the null-control arm's eval raises 1 bash syntax error on every run (the 'eval: syntax error: unexpected end of file' tail of each prepr.sh --self-test), and the pin 'step 1a3 lets a body naming this head run every step' passes on output produced after the parse failure.

title: N-reap-lock: an entry unload cancels its refresh but not the solve, so the reloaded entry's first solve waits out every orphan
claim: When an entry is unloaded (an options save reloads it) while a solve is in flight, async_shutdown cancels the refresh task awaiting coordinator._await_process but the executor thread keeps running _run_in_process under _PROCESS_LOCK, and nothing on the unload path reaps the worker, so the new entry's first job waits out the orphan's remaining time (ratio 1.00) and, after three reloads, out three whole orphaned solves (17.0 s behind 6 s jobs, 2.83x one job).

title: Scalar Carnot flow-lift factor is inverted: a hotter flow raises COP, and the batch twin disagrees
claim: ThermalModel.flow_lift_factor returns carnot_ref/carnot_flow (>1 above the 35 C reference, 1.586 at a 60 C flow and 0 C outdoor) while _batch_cop multiplies by carnot_flow/carnot_ref (<1), so every scalar COP priced at a flow above the reference (valved buffer, every DHW charge, a direct plant's curve) is boosted instead of derated and simulate_trajectory_batch disagrees with simulate_trajectory on 14 897 trajectory elements over the valved/combi/wood/coil arms. On the 50 published golden plans flow_lift_factor returned >1 on 1268 calls.
mechanism: thermal_model.py:3391 `return max(0.25, carnot_ref / carnot_flow)` against thermal_model.py:4483 `np.maximum(0.25, carnot_flow / carnot_ref)`. compute_cop (valve: flow_temp = tank), compute_cop_dhw (flow = tank water) and the curve-flow lift all route through flow_lift_factor; the batch twin, used for the solver's finite-difference gradient, carries the physical ratio. Consequences: the scalar objective prices hot storage cheaper the hotter it is (DHW COP 2.89 at 35 C, 4.26 at 55 C, 4.58 at 60 C at 0 C outdoor), and the gradient the solver follows is of a different physics than the objective it scores.

title: Scalar flow_lift_factor is inverted: lifting water hotter RAISES COP (up to 2.02x), breaking batch parity
claim: ThermalModel.flow_lift_factor returns max(0.25, carnot_ref/carnot_flow), which is >1 for every flow above the 35 degC reference, so compute_cop (valve plant, direct-plant curve) and compute_cop_dhw rise with flow/tank temperature on every climate, while the batch twin _batch_cop applies carnot_flow/carnot_ref.
mechanism: The ratio of two Carnot COPs is inverted in the scalar law only. carnot_flow < carnot_ref above the reference, so ref/flow > 1: a 55 degC hot-water charge is priced at 1.34-1.61x the space COP instead of 0.62-0.75x, a throttled buffer at the tank temperature likewise, and the Carnot fraction of the priced COP exceeds 1 (a COP above the Carnot limit) on 21320 grid points in four of five climates. _batch_cop uses carnot_flow/carnot_ref, so scalar and batch disagree by up to 8.01 COP units on the same inputs.

evidence.unit: count of adjacent (flow or tank) grid pairs where COP rises with flow, over 5 climates
evidence.machine: box B5 (shared compute box, linux x86_64, venv-ci python 3.14)
evidence.contention_note: counts only; box shared with up to two other seats

perturbation.change: thermal_model.py flow_lift_factor: `return max(0.25, carnot_ref / carnot_flow)` -> `return max(0.25, carnot_flow / carnot_ref)` (harness --perturb=lift, private copy)

metric_definition: Count of adjacent grid pairs (flow 20-70 degC step 0.5, tank 35-65, outdoor = climate range +-2 K, 241 pts) where compute_cop(valve) or compute_cop_dhw rises as flow rises, tol 1e-12.
phenomenon_property: Every flow/tank lift factor that prices COP is a derate in [0.25, 1] that is non-increasing in flow temperature, and scalar and batch COP laws agree bitwise on the same inputs.
proposed_fix_scope: thermal_model.py ThermalModel.flow_lift_factor: invert the ratio to carnot_flow/carnot_ref (the batch twin's form); every DHW and valve golden fixture drifts.

title: Measured defrost derate never derates: derate_from_duty adds duty x 1.5 and clamps to 1.0
claim: defrost.derate_from_duty returns min(1, max(0.55, 1 + duty*1.5)) instead of the module's documented 1 - duty*DEFROST_LOSS_MULTIPLIER, so every measured duty in (0, 0.30] yields 1.0 and a fully trusted 20 % defrost duty leaves the frost-band COP unchanged (ratio 1.0, documented 0.70).
mechanism: Sign error in the measured estimator. Because DERATE_MAX is 1.0 the result is pinned at 1.0; _decide hands the bucket to the measured estimator once duty_counts reaches DERATE_CONFIDENCE_SAMPLES, so on an install with a defrost flag the measured 1.0 also displaces any earned inferred derate: frost-band plans over-promise heat, the failure the module exists to stop.

evidence.unit: count of duty grid points (61 over [0, 0.30]) where derate_from_duty differs from the documented law
evidence.machine: box B5 (shared compute box, linux x86_64, venv-ci python 3.14)
evidence.contention_note: counts only; box shared

perturbation.change: defrost.py derate_from_duty: `1.0 + duty * DEFROST_LOSS_MULTIPLIER` -> `1.0 - duty * DEFROST_LOSS_MULTIPLIER` (harness --perturb=defrost, private copy)
perturbation.observed_value: duty_law_mismatch 60 -> 0; frost_cop_ratio 1.0 -> 0.70 on winter_mild (73 frost steps) and shoulder (41)

metric_definition: Count of duty points d in linspace(0, 0.30, 61) with |derate_from_duty(d) - clip(1 - 1.5 d, 0.55, 1.0)| > 1e-12.
phenomenon_property: A measured defrost duty d > 0 derates COP to clip(1 - d*DEFROST_LOSS_MULTIPLIER, DERATE_MIN, DERATE_MAX) < 1 wherever it applies.

null_control.value: winter_cold, summer_warm, summer_cool: frost_steps 0, frost_cop_ratio n/a; duty 0.0 point matches (1.0 both)
null_control.note: the identity is silent where no frost-band step exists and at zero duty

proposed_fix_scope: defrost.py derate_from_duty: subtract the duty term.

title: compressor_modulation=on_off is read as modulating: the declared on/off pump gets unclamped sub-p_min plans
claim: thermal_model.declared_modulation maps COMPRESSOR_MODULATION_ON_OFF to True (modulating) instead of False, so a user declaring an on/off compressor gets clamp_planned_levels False on every set-point unit, and the solve prices 32 of 96 steps at levels in (0, p_min) the pump cannot run; auto on the same surface clamps (0 such steps).
mechanism: Both explicit select values return True; the docstring and the options page say on_off -> False. Every reader inherits it: levels_clamped/duty_cycle_realizable (the plan's level law), learner_unmetered (the house learner's freeze) and probe_install(...).on_off. The explicit declaration is therefore weaker than leaving the key on auto.

title: price_risk_lambda's premium is booked as money: predicted_cost, baseline_cost, savings and prices carry lambda*sigma
claim: With price_risk_lambda > 0 the optimizer prices predicted_cost, baseline_cost, deferred cost and the published per-step prices on the risk-adjusted series, so predicted_cost != sum(raw price*power*dt) and the published saving is inflated by 12.46 currency at lambda 1 (25.06 at the config maximum 2.0) on the price_risk golden, where the thermostat baseline runs through the guessed tail the plan avoids.
mechanism: optimizer.optimize replaces prices with _stash_price_horizon's return (prices + lambda*sigma on unknown steps); every _Horizon closure (energy_cost_of) and _build_result (prices=h.prices) reads that array. The premium is a planning device (#34), never paid; the coordinator publishes predicted_cost/baseline_cost/predicted_savings and schedule[].price from the result and the accuracy promise (note_promise) reads result.prices.

evidence.contention_note: fan-out: up to three seats share the box; a count, contention-immune

metric_definition: savings_inflation = (baseline_cost - raw-priced baseline) - (predicted_cost - raw-priced plan spend), the published saving's gain from prices nobody pays
phenomenon_property: Every published money figure and per-step price of a plan is the raw input price series' (plus PV piecewise); a risk premium may shape the solve but never the reported spend, baseline or saving.

proposed_fix_scope: optimizer: keep the raw series beside the risk-adjusted one in _Horizon; price predicted/baseline/deferred and publish prices on the raw one

claim: price_model.prices_from_tibber_payload iterates period in ('today',) only, so a Tibber payload carrying today and tomorrow (96+96 quarter rows) returns 96 rows, and a plan solved at 14:00 knows 40 of its 96 steps instead of 96: the rest is filled from the learned prior.

title: The realised capacity tracker keeps each day's LOWEST window, so the billed peak and the capacity line are understated
claim: tariff._one_per_day keeps an entry when kw < best[day], so under distinct_days (the default) PeakTracker records each day's smallest closed window and billed_peak_kw reads 1.93 kW against 4.06 kW for three days of the winter_extreme capacity-tariff plan; 0.47-2.13 kW low on all 8 price shapes.
mechanism: tariff.py:491 `elif day not in best or kw < best[day][0]` (docstring: 'Each dated day's highest entry'). _close_window folds every closed window through it, so a day's recorded peak walks down to its quietest window; billed_peak_kw (ledger capacity line via book_capacity, the published billed peak) and threshold_kw (the plan's capacity threshold) both read the understated list.

title: The open month's coverage scale counts 744 h for the 743-hour March: a fully settled DST month reads 0.13 % high
claim: ledger.coverage_factor divides ledger.month_hours (days x 24, 744 for March 2026) by the settled hours, so a March settled for every one of its 743 real hours scales every estimated row figure by 1.001346 instead of 1.0.
mechanism: ledger.py month_hours ignores the DST hour (its docstring says so); coverage_factor = max(1, month_hours/settled). October (745 h) clamps to 1.0, so only the spring month is off; it lasts until the month closes.

title: A charge longer than one sample books its whole charge-start dip as a hot-water draw on every combi tank
claim: With no hot water drawn at all, dhw_learning.DhwProfileLearner books the 4 K charge-start dip of a 60-minute charge into DrawStats as 3.016 kWh of draw (2.459 kWh on internal_coil), the whole dip, on all three combi_tank constructions, because ChargeSettle.advance takes back only rises seen on UNHEATED intervals and the reading recovers while the charge is still heated; the one-sample charge the take-back was built for books 0.039 kWh.
mechanism: async_learn_dynamics folds every interval's beyond-standby drop into draw_stats (charge=started_heated or settling); the interval ending at the first heated sample is folded with charge=False (not provisional at all), and a dip on a later heated interval is provisional but ChargeSettle.advance returns 0 on every heated interval, so the recovery during the charge is never credited; the first unheated non-rise closes the charge with the dip still booked. The p90 ready target (dhw_draws.DrawStats.quantile) then asks the plan to hold more hot water than any draw needed.

evidence.unit: kWh
evidence.contention_note: fan-out, up to three seats on the box; an energy figure, contention-immune

perturbation.change: --perturb-skip-heated: async_fold_draw_stats books no fall on an interval that starts or ends on a heated sample

metric_definition: booked_kwh = sum of every DrawStats occurrence (closed + open) after a trace with zero real draw; identity 0 kWh
phenomenon_property: A fall of the tank reading that a charge's loading transient explains is never booked as draw, whatever the charge's length relative to the sampling interval and whether the dip lands on the first or a later heated sample.

null_control.note: the 'short' shape (one-sample charge, dip recovers unheated) books 0.039 kWh on every cell: the take-back works where it was designed to

reproduction_steps: Run the harness; read the long_a/long_b booked figures per combi_tank cell against dip_equiv
Re-run with --perturb-skip-heated: every booked figure goes to 0
proposed_fix_scope: dhw_learning: credit the dip's recovery across heated intervals of the open charge (or hold every charge-affected fall provisional until the charge closes), including the interval ending at the first heated sample

title: Ceiling-probe intervals metered at the pump's floor become the solve's learned top: the planned max drops 6.0 -> 1.5 kW
claim: draw_range.DrawRange.takes_ceiling accepts any experiment interval written at the ceiling whose draw clears idle, so 14 ceiling-probe intervals in which the load sat under the pump's minimum (drawn 1.5 kW, the floor) make draw_range.solve_band book max_kw 1.5 kW ('measured_below_configured') for a pump configured and truly able to draw 5.6-6.0 kW: a 4.10 kW narrowing below a draw the store never observed, while the uncensored arm keeps 6.0 and still learns a genuine 4.0 kW top.
mechanism: The store's median (learned_max_kw) is read as the pump's top with no test that the probe's draw was capacity-limited rather than load-limited; censoring at the modulation floor is indistinguishable from a small pump. solve_band then clamps every solve's max_electrical_power to it (for CEILING_LAPSE_DAYS, until CEILING_OVERDRAWS ordinary ceiling-written overdraws clear the store).

evidence.unit: kW
evidence.contention_note: fan-out, up to three seats on the box; a power figure, contention-immune

perturbation.change: --perturb-floor: takes_ceiling refuses a draw within AGREE_TOLERANCE of the window's metered running floor (DrawRange.observed()[0])

metric_definition: narrowing_kw = true pump top - solve_band(...).max_kw after the probe; identity 0 where the top was never observed
phenomenon_property: The draw range a solve books never falls below a draw the samples could not observe: a probe interval whose draw sits at the metered running floor (load-limited, censored) is no evidence of the pump's top.

null_control.note: samples=uncensored, true top 5.6: solve_max 6.0 (not_below_configured), narrowing <= 0; true top 4.0: learned 4.0, the honest narrowing the store exists for, kept under the perturbation

reproduction_steps: Run the harness; read samples=censored_at_minimum_power solve_max and narrowing_kw
Re-run with --perturb-floor: narrowing goes to 0, the uncensored top-4.0 cell still learns 4.0
proposed_fix_scope: draw_range: refuse (or mark censored) ceiling-store samples at the metered running floor / when the probe's delivered heat did not reach the commanded level; require evidence the draw was capacity-limited before solve_band lowers the top

title: The sysid adoption interval under-covers under 0.1 C quantisation and 0.02-0.05 C noise: 19 of 43 admitted fits miss it
claim: Under reading noise the fit is documented to tolerate (0.05 C white) and the 0.1 C quantisation of common room sensors, sysid.adoption_decision admits slab fits whose UA error exceeds the half-width it admitted them on in 9 of 11 (quantised) and 4 of 4 (white 0.05 C) cases, 19 of 43 over the three noisy arms against a nominal 0.05, all biased high (+7 % to +35 %), and the blend carries up to 11.7 % of UA error into house_heat_loss_scale from a learner sitting at the truth; noise-free windows recover UA to 5e-14.
mechanism: slab_ua_adoption_halfwidth combines the profile-likelihood and prior widths in quadrature, both conditional on the reading noise being white with the fitted residual scale; a quantised or larger-noise room series leaves the room temperature (a regressor in the slab fit) noisy, which biases UA upward (errors-in-variables) while the profile width shrinks with the residual fit, so the narrowest (admitted) intervals are the biased ones.

evidence.unit: count (quantised_0.1C admitted fits missing their interval, of 11 admitted)
evidence.contention_note: fan-out, up to three seats on the box; seeded counts, contention-immune

perturbation.change: --perturb-bar5: sysid.UA_ADOPTION_HALFWIDTH_BAR = log(1.05)

metric_definition: misses = admitted fits with |log(UA_fit/UA_true)| > the adoption half-width they were admitted on (95 % interval non-coverage; nominal share 0.05)
phenomenon_property: An admitted sysid fit's adoption interval covers the true UA at its nominal rate under every reading-noise model the fit is built for (white to 0.05 C, 0.1 C quantisation, slow drift), and the blend weight never carries a bias larger than the interval states.

null_control.note: noise-free and 0.005 C white: the interval covers at (better than) nominal; the defect appears only as noise grows

reproduction_steps: Run the harness (about 10 min on a loaded box); read RESULT *_misses and *_admitted per noise kind and the per-cell CELL lines

Leave-one-out over the 10 plant x noise cells with admissions (white_0.02, white_0.05, quantised_0.1C): miss share 19/43 = 0.44; dropping the most favourable cell (white_0.02 s_true 1.25 cr 1.4, 5/5) leaves 14/38 = 0.368
Re-run with --perturb-bar5: every admitted and missed count goes to 0
proposed_fix_scope: sysid: widen the adoption interval for regressor noise (quantisation variance d^2/12, residual autocorrelation) or test the fit's residual whiteness before admitting; a bias check against the declared plant before blending

title: A genuine internal gain is learned at 54-57 % of its size; the heat-loss scale absorbs the rest (-2.75 %)
claim: Driven together on a converged house with a genuine +0.6 kW evening gain (17-22 h) and zero-mean sensor noise, coordinator._fold_internal_gains settles the profile at 0.540-0.569 of the genuine gain over 15 noise x seed cells, while learner_newton_step moves house_heat_loss_scale to 0.9725 (truth 1.0) because both learners fold the same residual; with no genuine gain the profile stays within 0.009 kW of the prior and the scale within 1e-4.
mechanism: _fold_internal_gains steps g += INTERNAL_GAINS_ALPHA*y - INTERNAL_GAINS_RIDGE*(g - g0) on the residual power y left after the live model (which carries the profile through _model_corrections), so its own fixed point is only alpha/(alpha+ridge) = 0.714 of the gain; the share it leaves unexplained is folded into the heat-loss scale on the same interval, which reads extra evening heat as a tighter house and, by lowering UA, explains part of the gain away from the profile (scale and a near-uniform gain offset are near-collinear under a 6 K diurnal swing).

evidence.unit: ratio (learned gain / genuine gain, mean over 3 noise arms x 5 seeds)
evidence.contention_note: fan-out, three seats on the box; seeded arithmetic, contention-immune

perturbation.change: --perturb-ridge0: coordinator.INTERNAL_GAINS_RIDGE = 0

metric_definition: gain_recovery = mean over the gain hours of (learned profile g_h - prior g0) / (genuine gain), after 120 days of accepted dark intervals; identity 1
phenomenon_property: On a converged heat-loss level, the internal-gains profile converges to a genuine hour-correlated gain and the heat-loss scale stays at the true UA: no learner settles on a fraction of a covariate the other learner absorbs.

null_control.value: no-gain arm: gain_spurious_max 0.0092 kW (white), 0.0046 kW (quantised); scale_bias_nogain_mean +0.0001 (white, quantised)
null_control.note: with no genuine gain neither learner moves under zero-mean noise; the shortfall and the scale bias appear only with a genuine gain

reproduction_steps: Run the harness (about 1 min); read the CELL lines' gain_recovery_mean and scale_bias_genuine_mean per noise arm
Re-run with --perturb-ridge0: gain_recovery_mean rises 0.557 -> 0.775 (the ridge share); the rest is the scale's
The drifting arm's +0.06 scale under a +1.5 K outdoor drift is the scale reading a biased covariate (expected) and is not the claim
proposed_fix_scope: coordinator: fold the gains profile as a zero-mean shape about the level the heat-loss scale owns (or fold the scale on the residual after the profile's hour term), and drop the ridge's bias at the fixed point (shrink the step, not the target)

title: Import-level closures select 9 scripts (525.7 s recorded) for a payload.py function-body edit none of them executes
claim: Of the 170 (script, D3-s2 cell) closure pairs whose traced unmutated run is clean, 29 claim a cell whose function bodies the script never executes and never reads as text, so closure.py select runs that script for any function-body-only edit of that cell although the edit cannot change its run; payload.py alone carries 525.7 s of 3051.3 s recorded selected seconds this way (boost_drift_replay.py 341.1 s, optimality.py 142.5 s, validate.py 21.5 s, guard_pins.py 8.2 s, manual_plan.py 6.5 s, ...).
mechanism: tests/closures.json records the files a run imported or opened (derive_closures.sh); a module imported for its constants or a type is a closure member even when no function of it runs. tests/mutation_table.py already exploits the finer fact (reach_skip / never_reaches) for mutants, but the scoped gate's selection does not.

evidence.unit: over-approximated (script, cell) pairs of 170 clean pairs
evidence.machine: box B2, 4 cores, shared with D0-s2 and D9-s2
evidence.contention_note: count from traced baselines (mutation_table.traced_baseline, run by prescreen.py); contention-immune; the seconds weights are tests/closures.json's recorded seconds, not measured here

instrumented_symbol: tests/mutation_table.py:traced_baseline/collect/reach_problems over tests/closures.json:closures (the selection tests/closure.py select reads)

title: temperature_from_c is not the inverse of normalize_temperature_c: every Fahrenheit set-point write is wrong

title: project_window_mean never reads `remaining`: the peak guard weights the live draw by elapsed time
claim: power_guard.project_window_mean stores `remaining = window_minutes - elapsed` and returns (mean * elapsed + current_kw * elapsed) / window_minutes, so a constant 4 kW draw projects 0.0 kW at the window's start, 0.67 kW at minute 5 and 8.0 kW at minute 60 instead of 4.0 kW throughout.
mechanism: The dead local is the term the formula needs: the remainder of the window is assumed to continue at current_kw, i.e. current_kw * remaining. With `elapsed` in its place the projection under-reads for the first half of every metering window (the guard cannot suppress electric DHW before the peak is booked) and over-reads in the second half (it suppresses on a draw that is under the threshold). The docstring's own two limits fail: 'at the window's start this is the current draw' reads 0, 'at its end it converges on the realised average' reads mean + current. title: `The plan step covering now` is written four times; two copies have no end rule and hold the last step forever

title: Three small rules have copies that disagree: water's heat capacity, a naive instant's zone, a finite number

title: tariff._exact_topk_sum sums the k smallest excesses: the scalar capacity charge and its batch twin disagree
claim: tariff._exact_topk_sum returns sum(sort(excess)[:k]), the k smallest values, where its docstring and its batch twin (`np.sort(x, axis=1)[:, -k:]`) take the k largest; for every k above 1 with more than k windows the scalar _plateau_aware_topk_sum differs from _plateau_aware_topk_sum_batch (4 of 12 probes), peak_cost_smooth from peak_cost_batch (1 of 4), and the solve's scalar objective from objective_batch under a per-window capacity tariff (2 of 8, relative difference 1.4).
mechanism: The rule `the billed top-k` is written twice: once as tariff._exact_topk_sum (tariff.py:916), which the exact published charge peak_cost (tariff.py:1038) and the solver's scalar term _plateau_aware_topk_sum (tariff.py:958) call, and once inline in _plateau_aware_topk_sum_batch (tariff.py:943), which the batched objective calls for the finite-difference gradient. The scalar copy slices the wrong end of the sort. With [1, 5, 3, 4, 2, 0.5] and k = 2 the scalar returns 1.5 and the twin 9.0. It bites whenever more than k excesses are compared with k above 1: `Peaks on different days` off (peak_tariff_distinct_days False, the per-window rule the option's own text names), or a horizon spanning more plan days than peak_count. There the published projected_peak_cost bills the smallest excesses (often 0), and the solver's line search reads a capacity term its gradient was not taken from. On the default (distinct days, 3 peaks, a horizon of at most 3 days) k equals the number of day peaks and the two ends of the sort are the same sum, which is why the objective pair agrees there.

title: emitter_delivery lost its never-negative clamp: behind a valve the scalar model and its batch twin diverge
claim: mixing_valve.emitter_delivery returns ua * (mix_temp - zone_temp) with no floor at zero, against its own docstring (`Never negative: a valve can shut, but it cannot cool a house`) and against the inline np.maximum(0.0, ...) of simulate_trajectory_batch; under every throttling valve mode simulate_trajectory and simulate_trajectory_batch then diverge once the tank falls to the zone it feeds (18 of 42 probes, buffer temperature up to 2.4 K apart within 24 h), where they are bitwise equal on all 24 probes without a valve.
mechanism: The rule `what an emitter circuit takes from the mixed flow` is written twice: mixing_valve.emitter_delivery (mixing_valve.py:133), which the scalar two-zone step calls through thermal_model._valve_two_zone_delivery (thermal_model.py:2526, 2536), and inline in the batched trajectory (thermal_model.py:4673-4678). The scalar copy has no clamp, so with the pump off and the tank drained to the slab's temperature the scalar step moves heat from the slab back into the tank (slab 23.01 against the twin's 23.06 after one hour, tank 22.11 against 21.34): a mixing valve run in reverse. simulate_step is the model the coordinator predicts with and the solver's scalar objective integrates; the batch is what its finite-difference gradient is taken on, and the batch docstring states `bitwise parity is the contract`. On a valve install the objective and its gradient are therefore two different plants over every coast.

title: The presence rule for two zones is dead code: `auto`, the default mode, is resolved as `on`
claim: ThermalParameters.from_config tests the two-zone mode with `in (TWO_ZONE_MODE_ON, DEFAULT_TWO_ZONE_MODE)`, and DEFAULT_TWO_ZONE_MODE is `auto`, so every entry with no mode key or with `auto` is modelled two-zone whatever keys it holds; the `else` arm that infers the mode from the zone keys is reached only by an unknown mode string. On 4 of 6 configs the default mode and an unknown mode -- which the function's own comment declares the same rule -- give different answers.
mechanism: thermal_model.py:1122-1134: `if two_zone_mode in (ON, DEFAULT): True / elif == OFF: False / else: any(zone key in config)`. The three arms take all three values of const.TWO_ZONE_MODES between them, so the presence rule above them in the comment (`auto ... is the presence rule unchanged; an unknown value is treated as auto`) cannot run for a valid entry. An install that never chose a mode and stores no zone keys -- every single-zone house set up before the mode key, and tests/profiles.py's `house(two_zone=False)` -- is simulated, planned and identified as two zones with the default zone parameters. config_flow._single_zone takes its answer from the same call, so the options flow hides the whole-house loss field on those entries too.

title: Card HistorySource never trims rows past its 48 h span: retained rows grow linearly with the card's life
claim: On a long-lived card element whose plan dialog is panned into the past once a day, HistorySource retains 1,448 more rows per day (log 476, actionLog 152, seen keys 628, memoized overlay points 192; 60 covered chunks after 30 days against a 48 h reach of 4-5), with no plateau, while its own HISTORY_SPAN_MS caps what it can ever show at 48 h.
mechanism: HistorySource is built once per card element (constructor) and survives every dialog session (ViewWindow.onDialogClosed resets only the range). absorb() appends every fetched row to this.log[field], this.actionLog and this.seen, and fetchChunk adds each chunk to this.covered; ensure() deletes only the stale live-edge chunk's 'loaded' mark. Nothing drops a row older than Date.now() - HISTORY_SPAN_MS, and overlays() re-materialises one point per plan step of every covered chunk into this.memo, so the memo also grows per day.
